full_judgment:
AKM Fazlur Rahman J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 13-8-2000 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Khulna in Sessions Case No. 172 of 1998 convicting the appellant and absconding accused Ful Banu under sections 314/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 10,000 each, in default, to suffer further rigorous imprisonment for one year. 

 2. Short prosecution case is that on 12-8-1928 appellant Raqib without the consent of his wife, deceased Anowara with intent to cause her miscarriage got a piece of root of plant placed in her vagina by absconding convict Ful Banu resulting in profuse bleeding from her private parts and miscarriage. Then on 13-8-1998 he got his wife admitted into Terakhada Upazila Health Complex where she died on 14-8-1997 at 5-10 AM due to haemorrhage. 

 3. Dr Muniruzzaman, a medical officer of the hospital, in writing informed the local police station about unnatural death of the deceased in the hospital, on the basis of which UD Case No. 14 of 1997 dated 14-8-1997 was recorded and SI Mosharraf Hossain, attached to that police station going to the hospital made inquest of the dead body of the deceased and sent the same to the morgue for post mortem examination for ascertaining cause of her death. Autopsy of the dead body was held by Dr Golam Mortuza, who opined that death of the deceased was due to hemorrhage resulting from abortion. Then SI Mosharraf Hossain, the investigating officer of the UD case, on 25-9-1997 lodged First Information Report against the appellant and absconding convict Ful Banu with the accusation of causing death of the deceased doing some act intending to cause her miscarriage. He himself investigated the case and after investigation submitted charge-sheet against the appellant and absconding convict Ful Banu. They were put to trial in the 4th Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Khulna, wherein charge under sections 304 and 314 of the Penal Code was framed against them to which the appellant on dock pleaded innocence and claimed justice. Trial was held in absence of absconding accused Ful Banu. 

 4. The defence case, as it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses and also from the evidence adduced by the defence, is that of innocence and false implication. Positive defence taken by the appellant is that in his absence and behind his knowledge the deceased caused her miscarriage through absconding accused Ful Banu, that on 13-8-1997, mother of the deceased took her from the appellant's house to her house, that when the deceased was living in her parent's house, at the instance of her mother accused Ful Banu caused her miscarriage and thereafter she was shifted to the hospital where she died. 

 5. At trial, in order to prove the charge, the prosecution examined as many as nine witnesses, of whom five, namely, PW 1 and PW 8 SI Mosharraf Hossain, PW 2 Dr FM Muniruzzaman, PW 3 constable Faruque Hossain, PW 5 Taslima Khatun and PW 6 Dr Golam Mortuza are official witnesses. SI Mosharraf Hossain, the investigating officer of the UD case, the informant and investigating officer of the instant case was examined twice, once as PW 1 and then as PW 8. PW 2, the medical officer attached to Terakhada Upazila Health Complex, informed the police station in writing as to the unnatural death of the deceased in the hospital. PW 3 is the constable, who escorted the dead body of the deceased to the morgue for post mortem examination, PW 5 was a nurse of Terakhada Upazila Health Complex and PW 6 Dr Golam Murtaza held autopsy of the dead body. The remaining four are local and private witnesses, of whom PW 4 Abdul Mannan Fakir and PW 7 Md Shahidullah are the neighbours of the appellant, while PW 9 Mohammad Ali is the father of the deceased, PW 10 Kawsar Chowdhury is a seizure witness. 

 7. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant, having taken us through the impugned judgment and order, the First Information Report, the charge, the, depositions of the prosecution and defence witnesses and other materials on record makes his submission supporting the appeal and assailing the impugned judgment and order. He submits that the prosecution failed to prove the charge against the appellant beyond all reasonable doubt. There is no convincing evidence that at the instance of the appellant miscarriage of his deceased wife was done which resulted in her death. None of the prosecution witnesses had direct knowledge that the appellant with intent to cause miscarriage of his deceased wife got a root of plant placed in her uterus by absconding convict Ful Banu. The evidence of PW 5 shows that the deceased had consent in causing her miscarriage. The Court below wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant under section 314 of Penal Code, who is entitled to get acquittal. 

 8. Mr Md Faisal Hossain Khan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General with Mrs Parvin Hannan, the learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondent, opposes the appeal supporting the impugned judgment and order. He submits that by the uncontroverted evidence of PW 9, the father of the deceased, it is well proved that the appellant without the consent of his deceased wife with intent to cause her miscarriage got herb placed in the uterus of the deceased by absconding convict Ful Banu and thereby caused abortion, which resulted in her death. The defence taken is after thought and got up and also not proved. Such defence case had not been suggested in cross- examination to the PWs. At last stage of the trial a new story was advanced through the mouths of the DWs. Even the appellant at the time of examination under: section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure did not disclose such defence case. Such belated defence case is doubtful. The Court below rightly and legally convicted the appellant. Therefore, there is no ground for interference with the impugned judgment and order. 

 10. PW 1 and PW 8 SI Mosharraf  Hossain, the informant and the investigating officer of the present case and also the investigating officer of the unnatural death case, deposed that on 14-8-1997, while he was attached to Terakhada Police Station as sr of Police he received a report from Dr Muniruzzaman, medical officer of Terakhada Upazila Health Complex, to the effect that a woman named Anowara Begum died in the hospital due to hemorrhage. On the basis of that information he recorded Terakhada Police Station UD Case No. 14 of 1997 dated 14-8-1997 and himself took up investigation of the case. He rushed to Terakhada Upazila Health Complex taking constable Faruque Hossain with him, where in presence of the witnesses and the nurse on duty made inquest of the dead-body of the deceased as identified by PW 9, the father of the deceased. At that time the nurse recovered a piece of root of plant from the uterus of the dead body and gave the same to him, which he seized under a seizure list. Then for ascertaining cause of death he sent the dead body of the deceased to the morgue for post mortem examination through constable Faruque Hossain. He came to know from the post mortem examination report .that the deceased died due to haemorrhage resulting from abortion. Then he ending the UD Case lodged First Information Report against the appellant and absconding convict Ful Banu accusing them for causing her miscarriage, which resulted in her death. He proved the First Information Report written by him which was marked as Exhibit 1. Sayed Ahmed, the officer-in-charge of the police station, on receipt of his written First Information Report recorded the case filling up prescribed First Information Report form. He arrested the appellant from his house under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in connection with the UD case. When he (PW 1) went to the hospital the appellant was not present there. On investigation he found that miscarriage was done against the will of the deceased. He further stated that he visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map, Exhibit 8 with separate index, Exhibit 9, recorded the statements of the witnesses under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and then after completion of investigation submitted charge-sheet against the appellant and absconding convict Ful Banu. 

 13. PW 4 Abdul Mannan Fakir deposed that on 14-8-1997 at 12-00 noon he heard that deceased Anowara Begum died at Terakhada Upazila Health Complex due to hemorrhage. But he did not know the cause of such haemorrhage. He was declared hostile and cross-examined by the prosecution. In cross-examination he stated that he was a neighbor of the husband of the deceased. He denied the suggestion that the accused husband through absconding convict Ful Banu against the will of the deceased caused her miscarriage, which resulted in her death due to haemorrhage. 

 16. PW 7 Md ShahiduIIah deposed that the appellant was his neighbour. On 13-8-1997 the deceased was staying in the house of her appellant- husband Raqib Sheikh. At about 10-00/10-30 AM he came to know that there was profuse bleeding from the genital organ of the deceased. Then he along with the accused, his father and mother carried the deceased to Terakhada hospital and got her admitted there. She was given treatment. On his query accused Raqib said to him that his wife Anowara with intent to cause miscarriage asked him to bring herbal medicine and to take her to the house of accused Ful Banu. Later on through accused Ful Banu herb was placed in the uterus of Anowara on 12-8-1997 in the house of accused Ful Banu. Taslima, the nurse, in the hospital at the time of washing the uterus of the deceased, recovered that herb. Anowara died in the hospital on 14-8-1997 at 5-10 AM. In cross-examination he stated that he had talk with Anowara lastly at 4-00 PM while she was lying on the bed in the hospital. She admitted to him about her abortion. At that time Mohammad Ali (PW 9), father of Anowara, was present. He volunteered that Anowara was not willing to cause miscarriage: 

 17. PW 9 Mohammad Ali, the father of the deceased, identifying his signature in the inquest report said that inquest of the dead body of the deceased was made in his presence in the hospital by the Daroga on 14-8-1997 at 3-00/4-00 PM. Anowara told him that her husband accused Raqib taking her to the house of accused Ful Banu got a herb placed in her uterus. He further said that a piece of root of plant, measuring 8/9 fingers in length, was recovered from the uterus of Anowara in his presence. Then Anowara died. Accused Raqib put pressure on Anowara, who was not willing to miscarriage her first conception. The appellant forcibly caused the miscarriage. In cross- examination he stated that before marriage there was affair between accused Raqib and the deceased. Raqib, his parents and he (PW 9) got the deceased admitted in the hospital. He volunteered that he deposed the truth. He never told lie. Accused Raqib compelled the deceased to use the herb. 

 19. DW 1 Gous Sheikh, elder brother of accused Raqib, deposed that the deceased was pregnant of 3/4 months. On 13-8-1997 mother of Anowara coming to their house took away Anowara to their house and later on Anowara was admitted into the hospital. On 13-8-1997 he went to Anowara in the hospital and heard that mother of Anowara through accused Ful Banu applied herb for causing miscarriage. 

 20. DW 2 Mosharraf Hossain Chowdhury deposed that Anowara had affair with accused Raqib before their marriage. Anowara was pregnant of 3/4 months. On 13-8-1997, mother of Anowara took away Anowara from her husband's house and then taking her to village Joysona caused her miscarriage and then got her admitted into the hospital. Raqib used to call him mama. His house was three hundred cubits away from the house of Raqib. He did not see mother of Anowara to take away Anowara to Joysona. 

 21. DW 3 Nurul Hoque Chowdhury said that before marriage Anowara had affair with Raqib. Their marriage took place in the house of Raqib. After marriage the deceased used to live in the house of her husband. The father of Anowara did not visit the house of Raqib. Anowara was pregnant and there was miscarriage. 

 22. These are all of the material evidence adduced by both the parties, on consideration of which we find that undisputedly on 14-8-1997 at 5-10 AM deceased Anowara died at Terakhada Upazila Health Complex, where she was under treatment of profuse bleeding from her private parts. On that very days PW 2, a medical officer attached to that hospital, in writing informed Terakhada Police that Anowara, a patient, under treatment in the hospital suffering from septicemia due to critical abortion died at 5-10 AM. On the basis of that report Unnatural Death Case No. 14 dated 14-8-1997 of Terakhada Police Station was recorded. PWs 1 and 8 the investigating officer of the UD case, going to Terakhada Upazila Health Complex made inquest of the dead body of deceased Anowara as identified by her father PW 9 Mohammad Ali and sent the same to the morgue for post mortem examination through PW 3 constable Faruque Hossain. PW 3 testified that he escorted the dead body of deceased Anowara to the morgue for post mortem examination and identified the same to the doctor. PW 6 testified that he held autopsy of the dead body of the deceased, Anowara brought and identified by PW 3. He found presence of clotted blood inside the vagina, perforation at the fundal region of uterus and presence of product of conception and clotted blood inside the uterus. He opined that death was due to shock and haemorrhage resulting from abortion, which was ante-mortem. Such evidence of the doctor as to the cause of death of the deceased had gone unchallenged. Moreover, such medical evidence as to cause of death does not suffer from any infirmity or inherent defect. Thus, it is well proved that abortion was the cause of death of the deceased. Now the question is whether such abortion which resulted in her death was natural, that is, act of God, or caused by any human. 

 23. PW 5, the nurse of the hospital where the deceased was under treatment at the time of her death, testified that on 13-8-1997 with profuse bleeding from the vagina the deceased was brought to the hospital by her accused-husband. On her query the deceased told her that there was a piece of root of plant placed in her uterus. She PW 5 then recovered the root of plant from her uterus. She handed over that piece of root of plant to PW 1, who seized the same. She identified the piece of root, Material Exhibit I, in the trial Court. PWs 1, 7 and 9 also supported recovery of the piece of root Material Exhibit 1 from the uterus of the deceased by PW 5. Thus it is proved that placing Material Exhibit I (a piece of root of plant) in the uterus abortion was caused. It was a human act. Someone placed the root of plant in the vagina of the deceased with intent to cause her miscarriage. We also find support of it from PW 7 who said that the appellant- husband told him that his deceased wife asked him to bring herbal medicine for causing miscarriage and asked him to take away her to accused Ful Banu for causing miscarriage. On 12-8-1997 a piece of root of pant was penetrated in her vagina. PW 9, the father of the deceased, also supported causing of miscarriage penetrating root of plant in the uterus. Thus it is established that someone caused abortion of the deceased which resulted in her death and an offence punishable under section 314 of the Penal Code was committed. 

 24. On careful examination, scrutiny and critical analysis of the evidence on record we find that there is no ocular evidence. No one of the prosecution witnesses saw the appellant to get the root of plant, material Exhibit 1, placed in the uterus of his deceased wife by absconding convict Ful Banu against the will of the deceased resulting in her miscarriage and ultimately causing her death. 

 26. PW 7 said that on 13-8-1997 at 10-00/10-30 AM he came to know that there was bleeding from the private parts of the deceased. Thereafter, he along with the appellant and his parents shifted the deceased to the hospital and got her admitted there. On his query appellant Raqib told him that his wife asked her to bring herbal medicine for causing miscarriage and requested him to take her to the house of accused Ful Banu. The root of plant was penetrated in the private organ of the deceased by accused Ful Banu in her house on 12-8-1997. The deceased admitted causing of abortion. 

 27. PW 9 gave evidence that on 13-8-1997 at 3-00/4-00 PM the deceased told him in the hospital that her husband accused Raqib taking her in the house of Ful Banu got a piece of root of plant applied in her private part by accused Ful Banu. She also told him (PW 9) that accused Raqib forcibly took away her to that house and that she was not willing to miscarriage her first conception. The above evidence of PW 9 had not been challenged in cross-examination. It was not said that deceased did not say so to him. Thus such evidence of PW 9 has gone unassailed. 

 28. At the time of cross-examination none of the PWs was suggested the story given by the DWs that the mother of the deceased taking the deceased to their house from the house of the appellant caused miscarriage of the deceased through absconding convict Ful Banu. No such positive defence case was adverted in cross-examination of the PWs. But by adducing DWs a new story was advanced by the defence that at the instance of the mother of the deceased miscarriage of the deceased was caused. Such belated defence version not supported by prosecution witnesses is unworthy of credit. The evidence given by DWs is unworthy of credit. 

 29. PW 7 said that the accused Raqib told him (PW 7) that his wife Anowara asked him to bring herbal medicine for causing miscarriage and asked him to take her to the house of accused Ful Banu, where on 12-8-1997 Anowara through accused Ful Banu penetrated a root of tree of plant in her uterus. PW 9 said that Anwara told him that accused Raqib took her to the house of Ful Banu and got the piece of root of plant placed in her uterus by Ful Banu. By their above evidence it is well proved that at the instance of accused-husband Raqib miscarriage was caused. Involvement of the appellant in causing miscarriage has been well established. At his instance miscarriage was done. 

 30. But from the evidence of PW 5 we find that the deceased wife was a consenting party. PW 5 is a disinterested and independent witness. She said that the deceased told her that she was pot ready to carry the child at that time. She did not want a child. The evidence given by PW 7 that Anowara was not willing to cause miscarriage is incredible. He is not supposed to know whether miscarriage was done against her will or with her consent. He did not say that the deceased told him that she had no consent or against her will forcibly miscarriage was caused. PW 9 also did not say that his daughter Anowara told him that she was unwilling to cause miscarriage or she opposed causing miscarriage or forcibly miscarriage was done by her husband against her will. PW 9 is not supposed to know whether the deceased was a consenting party or not. If Anowara had no consent it would not have been possible for the appellant to take her to the house of Ful Banu and forcibly to place the root of plant in her uterus. Moreover, she did not disclose to anybody that she had no consent. So, evidence given by PWs 7 and 9 that the deceased was unwilling to miscarriage and the appellant forcibly caused miscarriage suffers from infirmity and is unworthy of credit. 

 31. Having regard to the above finding we are of the view that the prosecution has been able to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the appellant with intent to cause miscarriage of the deceased got a piece of root of plant, Material Exhibit 1, placed in the uterus of the deceased by accused Ful Banu, which resulted in her death. The deceased wife had consent in such act of the accused husband. Therefore, we find that the appellant committed an offence punishable under section 314 Part 1 of the Penal Code. His act does not attract Part II of the same section. Maximum punishment under section 314 Part I of the Penal Code is imprisonment of either description for a term up to ten years with fine. The Court below wrongly sentenced the appellant to suffer imprisonment for life under section 314 of the Penal Code. Ends of justice will be met if the appellant is sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for five years under section 314 Part 1 of the Penal Code.
